## How this blog is built

Posts are written in Quarto. Nix supplies the build tools, and Pixi creates the shared R/Python environment used to run code. GitHub Actions renders the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages.

[How it works](architecture.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [View the source](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog){.btn .btn-outline-secondary target="_blank"}
:::

## From source to website

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "Each build renders HTML once. After publishing, changed automatic freeze results are saved for the next build."
flowchart TD
    A["main<br/>Quarto source + saved results"] --> B["GitHub Actions<br/>Nix + Pixi · one Quarto render"]
    B --> C["gh-pages → GitHub Pages<br/>HTML + assets for readers"]
    C -. "If automatic results changed" .-> D["Commit to main<br/>_freeze + manifest · skip ci"]
    D -. "Reuse on the next build" .-> A
```

## What is reproducible?

A `.qmd` file keeps a post's text, code, and figure definitions together in version control. During a build, Quarto can run the code or reuse saved execution results. Readers receive static HTML and browser-side components; the site does not need a running Python or R server.

::: {.callout-note}
`flake.lock` pins the Nix build tools. The R/Python environment is resolved through `pixi exec`, without a committed Pixi lockfile, so its package versions can change. Saved results also need to be refreshed when external data or computation changes; editing a dataset alone may not trigger a rerun.
:::

For implementation details, see [`_quarto.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/_quarto.yml), [`render-site.py`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/scripts/render-site.py), and [`publish.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml).
